question: What newly accessible capability is worth testing, and what might it change next?

sources.title: Replace with a primary paper, preprint, dataset, or official release
sources.rights_note: Public reference; do not copy protected text, figures, code, or media without permission.
sources.note: Prefer a primary source and record what it actually demonstrates.

sources.title: Replace with an independent check, executable oracle, or competing result
sources.rights_note: Use for verification and bounded analysis only.
sources.note: If no independent check exists, say so instead of upgrading the claim.

candidates.title: A short, searchable name for the lead
candidates.question: What exact question is still open after reading the sources?
candidates.claim: State the strongest claim without implying more evidence than exists.

human_direction.thought_experiment: What unusual scenario, analogy, or intuition is steering the search?
human_direction.cross_domain_bridge: Which other field supplies the productive comparison, and where might it fail?
human_direction.steering_question: What does the human want the formal work to explore?
human_direction.why_this_might_be_wrong: State the strongest reason the creative direction could be a false analogy.

formal_pressure.translation: Translate the intuition into a precise object, model, code task, or proof obligation.
formal_pressure.consequence_space: Enumerate the consequences, special cases, and predictions if the translation holds.
formal_pressure.counterexample_search: Describe the first counterexamples, adversarial cases, or competing derivations to run.
formal_pressure.oracle_scope: Say exactly what the oracle can establish and what it cannot.

empirical_boundary.what_compute_can_test: Which parts can be checked with mathematics, code, simulation, or existing data?
empirical_boundary.what_requires_reality: Which claims still require new measurements, experiments, or independent peer review?

status.independent_check: No check yet, or describe the check in plain language.

candidates.mechanism: What causal or computational mechanism could make this work?
candidates.bottleneck: What becomes scarce, difficult, or newly important if the claim holds?
unknowns: What result would falsify or substantially weaken the lead?
Which boundary condition has not been tested?

capability_test.task: Run the smallest reproducible math, code, simulation, or literature test.
capability_test.oracle: Define the exact check, invariant, proof obligation, baseline, or independent comparison.
constraints: Do not call a generated explanation a proof.
Preserve the input, version, seed, and failed attempts.
capability_test.artifact: A short notebook, executable test, counterexample search, or bounded negative result.

creative_test.task: Translate one verified relationship into a small original EPRS experiment.
creative_test.oracle: Listen or look for one specific change; technical validity is not creative approval.
constraints: Keep evidence, interpretation, and invention visibly separate.
Do not turn a scientific possibility into a public claim.
creative_test.artifact: One short audio, visual, or interactive study with a research note.

candidates.next_action: Choose the smallest test that can change the conclusion.

selection.method: external adapter plus human or agent review
selection.rule: Choose one lead; do not make every interesting paper into a song.

privacy.source_policy: Keep private notes, credentials, personal identities, and full copyrighted passages outside the public packet.
privacy.public_metadata: Publish only supported, rights-cleared descriptions; label speculation, creative inference, and failed tests.
